clue.text: Notice boring dock procession

indicators.note: to bore is to drill a hole into something, so what bores goes inside the other word rather than alongside it

parts.note: to dock a tail is to pare it, cutting it back, and the word splits open to take the other piece
a notice in a paper is an ad, the crossword's usual two letters for one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a slow morning at the harbour, where a dock is a quay. It is the other dock, the verb for cutting something short.
explanation.definitionFit: procession -> PARADE: a parade is a formal procession of people marching past, the noun for the march rather than for marching.

clue.text: Two princes and an unknown in formation

parts.note: P is the standard short form for prince, and Hal is the prince of Shakespeare's Henry IV — one behind the other
the article is taken at face value and joins the queue
algebra's unknown quantity is x, the letter you solve for

explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's Henry V before the crown, and the other prince is only his initial. The formation wanted is the Greek block of spearmen with shields locked.
explanation.definitionFit: formation -> PHALANX: a phalanx is a body of troops drawn up in tight ranks, so the definition names the arrangement they hold.

clue.text: Song for group with tenor fit for conference

parts.note: the song several voices sing in canon, each starting a line after the last — Frere Jacques is one
T is the standard short form for tenor on a score
someone fit for a job is able to do it

explanation.walkthrough: Two musical words in a row make the surface a choir practice, and only the first of them is a song. The furniture the phrase names belongs to this puzzle's king.
explanation.definitionFit: conference -> ROUND TABLE: a round table is a conference where every side meets as an equal, named for a table with no head to sit at.

clue.text: Six involved in endless caper by international artist

indicators.note: a caper that never ends loses the letter at its end — only the tail goes, not the whole word
someone involved in a business is caught up inside it, and that is where these two letters land

parts.note: to caper is to dance, and the last letter has been lopped off
the Roman numeral for six
I is the standard short form for international, as on a footballer's record

explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like an anagram signal and is a word for a dance instead. Leonardo is filed under where he came from, the Tuscan village of Vinci.
explanation.definitionFit: artist -> DA VINCI: definition by example, since Leonardo, who painted the Mona Lisa, is one named painter rather than a word meaning painter.

clue.text: Second half of Heston film follows technique of legendary Englishman

indicators.note: it wants only the back end of the title, the three letters after the hyphen

parts.note: the art of something is the technique of doing it — the art of conversation

indicators.note: it fixes the order, putting the piece in front of it second, behind what comes next in the clue

parts.note: Charlton Heston starred in Ben-Hur, and the back half of that title is what is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The film is the 1959 chariot-race epic, and the man defined at the end is the king this whole puzzle is built around.
explanation.definitionFit: legendary Englishman -> ARTHUR: the once and future king of British legend, counted English by tradition though the stories are Welsh in origin.

clue.text: Free, free, free at heart, uplifted with joint

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the two central letters are taken
letters set free are letters let out of the order they were given in, which is licence to rebuild the word
in a down entry, anything lifted up is read from the bottom of the grid towards the top

parts.note: the same four letters as the word before it, rebuilt into the ridge of coral a ship runs onto
the middle pair of that word is RE, and up the page it reads the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: Three frees in a row and each does a different job: one gives the instruction, one gives the letters, one gives up its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: joint -> REEFER: both are street words for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, so the definition swaps one piece of slang for another.

clue.text: The lady guarding a lake (the round one) is out of the woods?

indicators.note: a guard stands around whatever it protects, so the lady's letters close over everything else

parts.note: 'the lady' is her, and those three letters split apart to wrap the rest

indicators.note: here it is not a shape but a movement: the word before it goes around the word after it

parts.note: the article gives A, and L is the map-maker's short form for lake
one is I in Roman figures, with 'the' wrapped around it

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket holds a container inside a container, which is the whole difficulty. The question mark admits that being past the danger is not quite the same as being well.
explanation.definitionFit: out of the woods -> HEALTHIER: to be out of the woods is to be past the worst of an illness, which is to be in better health than before.

clue.text: Bread with gin drunk by revolutionary

indicators.note: a drunk has no idea what order his feet come in, and these letters lose their order the same way

parts.note: a roll is the small round loaf that comes with soup
the same three letters, stood in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread with gin drunk' paints a whole evening, but only one of those words is a synonym and the other is raw material. The definition is the single word at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: revolutionary -> ROLLING: taken literally rather than politically, something revolutionary turns over and over, which is what a barrel down a hill does.

clue.text: Punishment for toddler concerning watch from ages ago

parts.note: a time out is the naughty-step penalty handed to a small child
'of' does the same job: a book of birds is a book concerning birds
asked to mind the children, you watch them

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is old legal English for a right so ancient that no living memory reaches back to its start — nothing to do with the naughty step of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: from ages ago -> TIME OUT OF MIND: the idiom means from a point beyond anybody's memory, so far back that recall gives out altogether.

clue.text: Meat sauce for a gumbo's stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing is what sits inside something else, so the letters are packed within the words, in order and unbroken

parts.note: four consecutive letters straddle the join, starting at the end of one word and running into the next

explanation.walkthrough: Two cuisines in one line: gumbo is the Louisiana stew and the sauce wanted is Italian, so the food talk is misdirection and only the letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat sauce -> RAGU: ragu is the Italian sauce of minced meat simmered slowly with tomato, so the definition is a plain translation.

clue.text: Articulate men delivered sound messages

parts.note: to articulate a complaint is to voice it

indicators.note: a line is delivered when it is spoken aloud, so the word before it is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: men are males, and that word said aloud is spelt this other way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the signal for something heard and belongs to the definition instead; the word doing that job is 'delivered', which is what happens to a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: sound messages -> VOICEMAILS: they are messages recorded as sound and stored until played back, so the definition says what the things are made of.

clue.text: Virgin mother back from Bali hideaway

parts.note: ma is the informal word for mother

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, and that is all this takes out of what follows

parts.note: the last letter of the island's name
a den is the hideaway an animal or a schemer retreats to

explanation.walkthrough: The travel-brochure surface hides an ordinary charade, and 'back' is picking a letter rather than describing anybody's journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin -> MAIDEN: a maiden is an unmarried young woman, and the word keeps its sense of untouched or first in maiden voyage and maiden name.

clue.text: Charged in to vote for hoax, essentially

parts.note: to vote for a candidate is to elect them

indicators.note: the essence of a word is what sits at its core once the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: a hoax is a trick, and the three letters at the centre of that word are what remain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a rush to the polling station. 'Charged' is not the mood of the crowd but current in a wire, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged -> ELECTRIC: a charged wire is an electric one, and both words carry the figurative sense of an atmosphere crackling with tension.

clue.text: Sword, axe, club and fire essentially deployed

indicators.note: it asks for the essential core of the word before it, dropping whatever sits at either end
troops deployed are spread out into new positions, and letters treated that way keep none of their old order

parts.note: two more weapons hand over seven of the nine letters
the middle pair of that four-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: A list of weapons is exactly where a sword belongs, which is why the fodder hides so well: the first word is the definition and the rest is raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Sword -> EXCALIBUR: definition by example, since the named blade Arthur wields is one particular sword rather than a word meaning sword.

clue.text: Presenter of careless anachronism is missing

indicators.note: work done carelessly comes out in no particular order, and letters handled that way land anywhere
what has gone missing is taken out before anything else happens, so two letters leave the long word first

parts.note: the long word with the two letters of 'is' already taken out, ready to be reordered

explanation.walkthrough: An anachronism is a thing out of its own time, so the surface grumbles about a wristwatch in a period drama; the word itself is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenter -> ANCHORMAN: the anchorman is the presenter who fronts a news bulletin and hands over to reporters, holding it steady like a ship's anchor.

clue.text: Bird who keeps 17 advancing chess piece

indicators.note: a piece that advances moves towards the front, and that is where these four letters end up

parts.note: the piece the whole game is played to protect, sent forward to the head of the assembly
in Arthurian legend the wounded guardian of 17 has a two-word title; one half ends the bird, and the other, a royal rank and chess piece, is what is left

explanation.walkthrough: The keeper of the Grail is the Fisher King, and the clue swaps his two halves round. 'Bird' sits alone at the front and is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird -> KINGFISHER: the small brilliant blue river bird that hunts by diving for fish, so the definition is simply the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Chief swaggerer shown by sources of Chretien on chivalry? Kay

indicators.note: a source is where a thing starts, so each name that follows gives up only the letter it opens with

parts.note: four words in a row, each handing over the letter it begins with

explanation.walkthrough: Chretien de Troyes wrote the first Arthurian romances and Kay is Arthur's foster-brother, so the question in the surface is really a list of four initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief swaggerer -> COCK: the cock of the walk is the strutting top man of a group, the sense borrowed from the farmyard bird's bearing.

clue.text: Appeared before crowd in musical

indicators.note: it settles the order: what appeared is placed ahead of the crowd rather than behind it

parts.note: someone who appeared at the party came to it
a lot of people is a crowd of them, as in 'that lot outside'

explanation.walkthrough: The show's title later became the nickname for the Kennedy White House, and the castle behind it is the seat this puzzle keeps circling.
explanation.definitionFit: musical -> CAMELOT: definition by example, the 1960 Lerner and Loewe show about Arthur's court, named after the castle it is set in.

clue.text: Lady exhausted after beginning to hurdle over grand track for fabulous cup

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word that follows is wanted, not the word itself
a word exhausted has had its middle used up, leaving nothing but the letters at either end

parts.note: the first letter of the obstacle a runner clears
O is the cricket scorecard's short form for an over, the set of six balls a bowler sends down

indicators.note: it puts the emptied word behind the pieces already assembled rather than in front of them

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word, all that is left when the middle goes
G is the standard short form for grand
a railway track is a rail

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an athletics meeting, right down to the hurdle and the track, and every one of those sporting words is really an abbreviation or a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: fabulous cup -> HOLY GRAIL: the vessel Arthur's knights quest for, with 'fabulous' in its older sense of belonging to fable rather than wonderful.

clue.text: Petition for vote against stuck up Americans

indicators.note: the surface calls somebody snobbish; as an instruction it means the letters are pinned up the page and read from the bottom

parts.note: a vote against is a nay, and in a down entry it climbs the grid
to petition for a thing is to seek it, and those letters climb too

explanation.walkthrough: Both words are written out in clue order and the whole assembly is then read upwards, which is why the two halves seem to have swapped places.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans -> YANKEES: outside the United States a Yankee is any American at all, while inside them it means a northerner.

clue.text: First name shortened

definitions.meaning: the adjective: earliest, the opening one before any others
the noun: what is left of a name when only its starting letter is written

explanation.walkthrough: Three words that read as one phrase, a shortened first name, and the split falls after the very first word, with each half defining the same seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: First is the adjective sense, the opening one of a series; a name shortened is the noun, a name cut down to the single letter it starts with.

clue.text: See 15
Penguin could be leaving queen on island with hesitation for a big shop

indicators.note: whatever leaves is gone before the rest is used, and these two letters walk out of the middle of the bird

parts.note: the emperor is the biggest species of penguin, and 'could be' flags one example of the bird
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the crossword's usual queen, and these are the two letters that go
I is the standard short form for island on a map
um is the noise you make while you hesitate

explanation.walkthrough: Penguins and queens sit together so comfortably in the Antarctic surface that the instruction hides in plain sight; the rest is ordinary charade joinery saying what it means.
explanation.definitionFit: a big shop -> EMPORIUM: an emporium is a large store carrying a wide range of goods, the grand word a shop reaches for about itself.

clue.text: Discovered "in it" with donkey

indicators.note: to discover is to uncover what was already lying there, whole and in order, inside the words that follow

parts.note: six consecutive letters run from inside the quotation into the word after it, quotation marks and all

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks look as if they are flagging a phrase to work on. They are only there to hold the surface up, and the letters run straight through them.
explanation.definitionFit: donkey -> NITWIT: donkey has meant a fool for centuries, the animal's reputation for stubborn stupidity standing in for the person's, and the answer is the same insult.

clue.text: See 2
Cancels him after playing around? Not very likely

definitions.note: The definition is a phrase about how likely something is, while the answer is the noun phrase for the thing itself: what is not very likely is a slim chance.

indicators.note: to play around with something is to move it about with no plan, which is exactly what happens to these ten letters

parts.note: ten letters handed over whole, waiting to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is the setter admitting that his story of someone dropped after messing about is doing double duty as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Not very likely -> SLIM CHANCE: a chance called slim is a thin one, barely there at all, so the phrase names a low probability.

clue.text: British idea evens out French wheel?

parts.note: BR is the standard short form for British

indicators.note: the letters in even positions are the ones taken out, leaving every other letter counting from the start

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word, once the second and fourth have gone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens out' reads as smoothing something over and is really an instruction to throw letters away. The question mark covers a definition by shape, not by taste.
explanation.definitionFit: French wheel -> BRIE: the soft cheese from the Brie region is made and sold as a large flat round, so a wheel names it by its shape.

clue.text: Tough cockney fanatic turned around desolate region

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the aitch at the front of a word, so 'hard' is written without its first letter
an across entry turned around is read from its far end back to the start

parts.note: a fanatic is a nut, and the word is read here from its end
tough is hard, minus the aitch, and that too is read from its end

explanation.walkthrough: A hard nut is the tough customer the surface is describing, and the pair only work once the aitch has gone and the whole thing is read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: desolate region -> TUNDRA: the treeless Arctic plain where the ground never thaws, so the definition describes exactly the kind of place it is.

clue.text: A fop to boot

parts.note: the article is taken at face value and starts things off
Victorian slang for a dandy, the flashily dressed gentleman about town — the same word as a rising sea

explanation.walkthrough: Four short words, no indicator and no joke to unpick: the whole difficulty is seeing that the split falls after the very first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: to boot -> AS WELL: 'to boot' is an old idiom meaning in addition, from a Middle English word for advantage, so one whole phrase swaps for another.
